Theorem 1.1. — Let X be a strictly local, noetherian scheme of dimension d > 0, and let ℓbe a prime number invertible
on X. Then, for any open subset U of X, we have
(1.1.1)
cdℓ(U) ≤2d −1.
Recall that, for a scheme S, cdℓ(S) (ℓ-cohomological dimension of S) denotes the inﬁmum of the integers n
such that for all ℓ-torsion abelian sheaves F on S, and all i > n, Hi(S, F) = 0.
Corollary 1.2. — Let X = Spec A be as in 1.1, and assume A is a domain, with fraction ﬁeld K. Then
(1.2.1)
cdℓ(K) ≤2d −1.
Indeed, it sufﬁces to show that if F is a ﬁnitely generated Fℓ-module over η = Spec K, then Hi(η, F) = 0
for i > 2d −1. But η is a ﬁltering projective limit of afﬁne open subsets Uα of X, F is induced from a locally
constant constructible Fℓ-sheaf Fα0 on Uα0, and Hi(η, F) = lim
−→Hi(Uα, Fα), where Fα = Fα0|Uα for α ≥α0
([SGA 4 VII 5.7]).
Remark 1.3. — (a) The proof shows that, given X as in 1.1, with X integral, then, if (1.1.1) holds for any afﬁne
open subset U, (1.2.1) holds, too.
(b) If X is an integral noetherian scheme of dimension d, with generic point Spec K, and ℓis a prime number
invertible on X, then cdℓ(K) ≥d ([SGA 4 X 2.5]). Gabber can prove that under the assumptions of 1.2 one has
cdℓ(K) = d (see XVIIIB).

Theorem 3.1 (d)

Let \(f : X \to Y\) be an affine morphism of schemes of finite type over a field \(k\). Let \(F\) be a torsion sheaf on \(X\) such that \(d(F) \leqslant d\) (cf. 2.1). Then \(d(R^q f_* F) \leqslant d-q\).

In particular, taking \(Y = \operatorname{Spec}(k)\):

Corollary 3.2

Let \(X\) be an affine scheme of finite type over a separably closed field \(k\). Then

\[\operatorname{cd} X \leqslant \dim X \;.\]

Corollary 3.3

Let \(X \subset \mathbb{P}^N_k\) be a projective scheme of dimension \(n\) over a separably closed field \(k\), and let \(Y = H \cap X\) be a "hyperplane section" of \(X\). Then for every torsion sheaf \(F\) on \(X\), the canonical homomorphism

\[H^q_Y(X,F) \longrightarrow H^q(X,F)\]

is bijective for \(q > n+1\), and surjective for \(q = n+1\).

The corollary is trivial from 2.2 and the exact sequence for a closed subset (IV 3.7.1), taking into account that \(X - Y = \mathcal{U}\) is affine of dimension \(\leqslant n\).

Each reduced irreducible component \(Z_i\) of \(Z\) is then either an affine scheme of finite type of dimension \(\leqslant 1\) over the closed point \(y\) of \(Y\), or a quasi-finite scheme over a reduced closed subscheme \(C\) of \(Y\) of dimension 1.
Theorem 6.1 ^{(∗)}

Let \(f : X \to Y\) be an affine morphism of finite type, where \(Y\) is an excellent scheme of equal characteristic, and let \(F\) be an abelian torsion sheaf on \(X\). Then \(R^q f_* F\) is zero at each point \(y \in Y\) such that \(\delta(F,f,y) < q\).

The local variant, obviously equivalent to 6.1, is the following:

Theorem 6.1 bis ^{(∗)}

Let \(A\) be an excellent strictly local ring of equal characteristic, and \(f : X \to Y = \operatorname{Spec} A\) an affine morphism of finite type. Let \(F\) be a torsion sheaf on \(X\). Then \[H^q(X, F) = 0 \quad \text{if} \quad q > \delta(F).\]

Let \(A\) be a henselian, excellent ring of equal characteristic, with residue field \(k\), and let \(U \subset \operatorname{Spec} A\) be an affine open set. Let \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\). We have \[\operatorname{cd}_\ell U \leqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell k + \dim A.\]

Indeed, let \(\tilde{A}\) be the strict localization of \(A\), which is an infinite Galois étale covering, of group \(G = G(\bar{k}/k)\), and let \(\tilde{U}\) be the affine open set of \(\operatorname{Spec} \tilde{A}\) induced from \(U\). Applying the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence (VIII 8.4) \[H^p(G, H^q(\tilde{U}, .)) \Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(U, .)\] we are reduced to treating the case \(A = \tilde{A}\), and then it is a special case of 6.1 bis.

With the notations above, let \(R(A)\) be the ring of rational functions on \(A\). We have \(\operatorname{Spec} R(A) = \varprojlim_\alpha U_\alpha\) where \(U_\alpha\) is an affine open set of \(\operatorname{Spec} A\). It therefore follows from the theory of passage to the limit that we have

Corollary 6.3

Let \(A\) be henselian, excellent, of equal characteristic, with residue field \(k\). Let \(R(A)\) be the field of rational functions on \(\operatorname{Spec} A\). Then for \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\), we have \[\operatorname{cd}_\ell R(A) \leqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell k + \dim A\]

with equality if \(\ell\) is invertible in \(k\), and if moreover \(\ell \neq 2\) or \(k\) is not orderable.
Corollary 6.4

Let \(X\) be an excellent noetherian scheme of equal characteristic, and \(R(X)\) the ring of rational functions on \(X\). Let \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\) be invertible on \(X\), and suppose that \(\ell \neq 2\) or that no residue field of \(X\) is orderable. Then \[\operatorname{cd}_\ell(X) \leqslant \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(X) + \dim X \leqslant 2 \operatorname{cd}_\ell R(X).\]

Proof of 6.1. We begin with a reduction analogous to that of XIV 3. Induction on \(\delta\): It is clear that 6.1 for \(\delta \leqslant d\) is equivalent to (6.1 bis) for \(\delta \leqslant d\). For \(\delta = 0\), it is trivial. Let us treat the case \(\delta \leqslant 1\), in the form 6.1 bis. Since \(F\) is a limit of its constructible subsheaves (IX 2.9 (iii)), one may assume \(F\) constructible, and then the support of \(F\) is contained in a closed set \(Z \subset X\) with \(\delta(z) \leqslant 1\) for each \(z \in Z\) (XIV 2.2). Each reduced irreducible component \(Z_i\) of \(Z\) is then either an affine scheme of finite type of dimension \(\leqslant 1\) over the closed point \(y\) of \(Y\), or a quasi-finite scheme over a reduced closed subscheme \(C\) of \(Y\) of dimension 1. In this last case, we have \(C = \operatorname{Spec} B\) where \(B\) is an integral strictly local ring of dimension 1. Such a scheme \(Z_i\) is the spectrum of an integral strictly local ring, of dimension \(\leqslant 1\), or of a finite extension of the field of fractions of \(B\). Hence the cohomological dimension of \(Z_i\) is at most equal to 1 in any case, by X 2.3 and IX 5.7. We have an exact sequence \[0 \longrightarrow F \longrightarrow \prod_i F_i \longrightarrow \varepsilon \longrightarrow 0\] where \(F_i\) is the restriction of \(F\) to \(Z_i\), from which we draw the result for \(Z\).

**Theorem 1.1.3 (Gabber).** *Let X be a strictly local noetherian scheme of dimension d > 0, and ℓ a prime which is distinct of the residue characteristic of X. Then, for any open subscheme U ⊂ X, we have cdℓ(U) ≤ 2d − 1.*

For a proof, see [ILO14, Exposé XVIII_A, Theorem 1.1].

**Lemma 1.1.4.** *Let X be a noetherian scheme of dimension d. Then, for any sheaf of Q-vector spaces F over X_et, we have H^i_et(X, F) = 0 for i > d.*

*Proof.* Nisnevich cohomology and étale cohomology with coefficients in étale sheaves of Q-vector spaces coincide, and Nisnevich cohomological dimension is bounded by the dimension, which proves this assertion.

**Theorem 1.1.5 (Gabber).** *Let S be a strictly local noetherian scheme and X a S-scheme of finite type. Then X is of finite étale cohomological dimension, and the residue fields of X are uniformly of finite étale cohomological dimension.*

*Proof.* An easy Mayer–Vietoris argument shows that it is sufficient to prove the theorem in the case where X is affine.

Example 13.1 (affine and projective space). Let \(k\) be separably closed and \(\ell\) invertible in \(k\). Then

\[ \operatorname{cd}_\ell(\mathbf A^r_k)=r, \qquad\operatorname{cd}_\ell(\mathbf P^r_k)=2r. \tag{13.1} \]

The upper bounds are Theorems 5.1 and 4.1. Here is a proof that they are attained. Put \(j:U=\mathbf A^1\setminus\{0,1\}\to\mathbf A^1\) and \(Q=j_!\mathbf F_\ell\). The closed-open sequence gives

\[ H^1(\mathbf A^1,Q)=\operatorname{coker} (\mathbf F_\ell\xrightarrow{\mathrm{diag}}\mathbf F_\ell^2) =\mathbf F_\ell. \tag{13.2} \]

Indeed the constant affine-line cohomology has only degree zero by lesson 15, and each closed point is acyclic. The same sequence gives \(H^0(Q)=0\) and no higher groups. Apply Theorem 12.3 repeatedly to \(Q\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes Q\) on \(\mathbf A^r\): its degree-\(r\) cohomology is \(\mathbf F_\ell\). Thus affine cohomological dimension is attained by a nonconstant sheaf, even though the constant sheaf has no positive cohomology.
